title: Influence decomposition
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $f$ be real-valued on its outcome space, and choose a coordinate $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. The influence of $f$ at $i$ equals the sum, over all coordinate subsets $S$ containing $i$, of the expected squared $S$-component of $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses
$f$ is real-valued on the outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and a coordinate $i$. Then $I_i(f)=\sum_{S\ni i}\mathbb E_Pf_S^2$.
